claims.statement: Every data-channel message is a protobuf Message (ts-proto-generated from src/proto/message.proto) carrying a file id plus exactly one payload: metaData, chunk, or receiveEvent (ACCEPT/REJECT/RECEIVED_CHUNK/VALIDATE_ERROR).
File ids are crypto.randomUUID() values rather than filenames, so same-named files in one session keep distinct ids and their chunks never cross-wire; metaData.name is used for display only.

The sender maintains per-file state in a reactive map with lifecycle Pending -> WaitingAccept -> Processing -> Success; on ACCEPT it starts the chunk loop, on REJECT or VALIDATE_ERROR it records the error and resets the file to Pending (retryable); the async event handlers re-read the live entry after each await and bail if it was removed, and chunk-send failures land as visible error entries instead of unhandled rejections (via the shared markChunkFailed helper, deduplicated in PR #70); a connectionLost flag - a $state the template reacts to, NOT a $derived(channelSender.isLost()) which would cache false forever since isLost() reads a plain closure variable - is flipped by onChannelClose() and by a thin send() wrapper mirroring the helper's lost flag (PR #109), marking the channel as dead so in-flight pipelines exit quietly with accurate connection-lost errors instead of per-chunk InvalidStateError failures (PR #74, shared helper PR #97), and the SendingFileList UI hides the Resend/Continue/Send buttons (leaving only Remove) when the channel is lost because each would be a guaranteed silent no-op. Since PR #121 the EVENT_RECEIVER_ACCEPT handler additionally resets the closure clock fileStats.startTime = Date.now() next to the entry-level f.startTime = Date.now(), so the 'Sending: X/sec' bitrate divides by time-since-ACCEPT (mirroring the receiver's onAccept entry clock) instead of time-since-Send-click, which any waiting-accept delay would have inflated and grossly under-reported throughput. Since PR #137, onSend on the Resend path also resets the attempt-scoped progress to 0 (in addition to bitrate and startTime from PR #125), so a Resend no longer leaves the file's UI progress bar stuck at the prior attempt's percentage until the first acked chunk of the new attempt ticks the throttle (a first send is unaffected - onFilesPick registers progress: 0, so the reset is a no-op there).

The transfer protocol is receiver-ack chunking: the receiver enqueues each incoming chunk onto a per-file serialized chain (onChunkData), and processChunk sends EVENT_RECEIVED_CHUNK after successful decryption and a re-check that the file is still active, so the sender sends at most one next chunk per ack until offset reaches metaData.size - backpressure pacing the transfer with the sender one round-trip ahead.

A defensive empty-chunk guard aborts the send with an 'Invalid chunk size' error when a chunk reads 0 bytes while bytes remain, preventing an infinite loop of empty sends caused by an invalid chunkSize (e.g. a crafted 'c' URL param).

Progress and bitrate UI updates are throttled by PROGRESS_UPDATE_UI_STEP (3 percentage points) using non-reactive stats mirrors, and the per-file progress + bitrate write is now the shared updateTransferProgress(stats, sentBytes, totalBytes, writeTo) helper in src/utils/transferProgress.ts (PR #136, deduplicated from the copy-pasted blocks in Sender.sendNextChunk and Receiver.processChunk): it clamps progress to [0,100] with a NaN->0 fallback, computes bitrate = sentBytes / elapsed where elapsed is time-since-ACCEPT floored to a 1 ms minimum (PR #134), and advances nextProgressUpdate by PROGRESS_UPDATE_UI_STEP clamped to 100. Pause/resume is implemented via a per-file stop flag where onContinue re-emits a synthetic RECEIVED_CHUNK event to restart the chunk loop - except on a dead channel, where onContinue no-ops (channelSender.isLost() check) so a resume cannot emit a synthetic ack into a pipeline whose next send would just no-op.

The receiver keeps per-file chunk buffers, byte counters, and per-file processing chains in deliberately non-reactive plain objects (receivingFileChunkMap / receivingFileStatsMap / chunkQueue) so chunk arrival does not trigger Svelte re-renders; only the reactive receivingFiles map is flushed at the 3-point progress step.

On completion (receivedSize exactly equals the declared size) the receiver builds the file Blob immediately, deletes the per-file chunk/stats/queue maps AND, since PR #133, the receivingFileGeneration entry (a Success entry is terminal and a Success re-offer is ignored, so its generation can never matter again), releasing the raw per-chunk buffers so a large file is not held twice in memory.

validateFileMetadata is the single size gate and enforces three bounds because metaData.size is peer-controlled: a size that is not finite, is <= 0, or is not an integer (PR #127) is rejected with 'invalid file size' (a fractional size can never equal the integer sum of chunk byte lengths that the exact-match gate receivedSize === size compares against, so accepting it would complete then dead-end the transfer), and size > maxSize fails with a humanFileSize-rendered limit message (default 1 GB via DEFAULT_RECEIVE_OPTIONS, which stays below the largest offered Max Size of 2 GB that in turn stays under the classic-ZIP 4 GiB per-entry cap, so the default never allows a file the bulk 'Download all files (zip)' path cannot archive); receiver-side validation failure sends EVENT_VALIDATE_ERROR back to the sender and records the error on the file, while autoAccept (default true) makes the receiver accept valid files without user action.

The data channel is created ordered:false, so chunk ordering is enforced by the protocol (one receiver ack drives one sender chunk, isolated per file id) rather than by channel-level ordering; completion is exact-declared-size based with no trailer or checksum.

onMetaData sanitizes the peer-controlled MetaData.name via sanitizeName as its first action (PR #98 — one ingestion rule covering all sinks: the bulk store-only ZIP archive and <a download>) so a path-traversal name can no longer reach either sink; it then registers the file entry at WaitingAccept BEFORE the async AES key decryption, so the file is visible and removable throughout; if the RSA key unwrap fails, the entry gets a visible error, an error toast fires, and EVENT_VALIDATE_ERROR is sent to the sender (bouncing its file to Pending) instead of the file silently never appearing while the sender waits for an accept that will not come; the metadata-failed entry stays in WaitingAccept with the error shown, so it is not a Remove-only dead-end (PR #76) — but an Accept on it is refused by the onAccept guard (PR #78): explanatory toast plus EVENT_RECEIVER_REJECT, no state change, no chunk map, leaving Deny/Remove as the real exits (the PR #117 null+status guard runs before this reject branch without short-circuiting it — a WaitingAccept entry still reaches it).

Per-file chunk processing is serialized on a per-file promise chain (serializeTask): processChunk for chunk N+1 cannot start before chunk N's processing has settled, so decrypt/push/stats/blob-on-complete run in strict arrival order even when WebCrypto decrypt completions are out of order; the chain's catch routes any error to rejectCorruptChunk (idempotent — no-op once the per-file chunk map is gone) instead of swallowing it, so a failed chunk can never leave the file permanently incomplete or stall the queue.

Late or stray chunks are dropped, not fatal: onChunkData ignores chunks for unknown or uninitialized file ids (metadata never registered, file removed/denied, or already completed), and processChunk re-checks the chunk map after the decrypt await so a file removed/denied mid-flight is dropped without acking (an ack would advance the sender past a rejected file).

Bulk download builds a real store-only ZIP archive in memory (createZipStoreOnly: method-0 entries, CRC-32, UTF-8 name flag, duplicate-name disambiguation that checks each candidate against every already-emitted final name so pre-suffixed peer-controlled names cannot collide, no new dependency) and saves a single zero-share-files.zip via triggerDownload, instead of the former sequential per-file raw downloads that never produced a zip; onDownload null-guards the entry so a missing/duplicated key no longer throws an unhandled TypeError and skips the per-file teardown. Entry names are sanitized on the way in: Receiver.onMetaData runs metaData.name = sanitizeName(metaData.name) at ingestion (one rule covering all sinks), and createZipStoreOnly/uniqueNames re-sanitize each entry as defense in depth, so a peer naming a file with embedded path traversal (zip-slip / CWE-22) can no longer land verbatim in the archive — sanitizeName keeps only the safe basename (last segment across /, \\, and U+2215), drops NUL/C0 control/DEL, collapses dot runs, and falls back to 'file' on empty. The bulk zip is capped by the classic-ZIP per-entry ceiling: createZipStoreOnly writes no zip64 extra fields, so it throws explicitly when any entry is >= 4 GiB (0xffffffff) or the archive's central directory starts past that value, instead of emitting a silently corrupt archive (PR #110).

All receiver downloads route through triggerDownload, which defers URL.revokeObjectURL ~1 second after clicking the temporary download anchor, because revoking in the same tick can abort the async download in some engines (e.g. Firefox starting the fetch after the revoke).

MetaData.size is int64 on the wire (PR #42 / commit 721c502; was int32), so files of 2 GiB or larger no longer throw 'invalid int32' during Message.encode; tests/protocol-size.test.mjs pins this by encoding and round-tripping 3 GiB and MAX_SAFE_INTEGER sizes through the generated proto code.

The receiver 'Max Size' dropdown options carry true byte values matching their labels (10 MB = 10 * 1024 * 1024, 100 MB = 100 * 1024 * 1024, 1 GB, and 2 GB as the largest option); previously the 10/100 MB options were 1024x smaller than their labels and enforced KB limits (PR #44). The largest option is now 2 GB rather than the former '10 GB' and 'Unlimit' (1 TiB) options, because createZipStoreOnly writes no zip64 extra fields and so can never archive an entry of 4 GiB or larger — the old 10 GB / Unlimit values made the bulk 'Download all files (zip)' path silently impossible for their own allowed sizes (PR #110). onChange coerces the select value with Number(maxSize) and falls back to DEFAULT_RECEIVE_OPTIONS.maxSize when not finite, because bind:value on a <select> yields a string after user interaction, so ReceiveOptions.maxSize stays a number at runtime. tests/receiver-options-size.test.mjs statically pins these option values, the 4-GiB classic-ZIP ceiling on the largest option, and the coercion.

Chunk size is enforced numeric on two layers: Sender.sendNextChunk defensively coerces its chunkSize prop with Number() (32 KB fallback for non-finite/non-positive values) so a string from a <select> bind:value can no longer make offset + chunkSize concatenate and send the whole file remainder as one over-sized chunk, and OfferOptions.onChange coerces the select value with Number() and falls back to DEFAULT_SEND_OPTIONS.chunkSize when it is not in CHUNK_SIZE_OPTIONS, keeping sendOptions.chunkSize a number at the source.

A chunk that fails AES-GCM authentication is rejected visibly, not dropped: processChunk routes the decrypt failure to rejectCorruptChunk, which is generation-fenced (PR #125) and delegates to the shared rejectFile(id, receivingFile, error, toastMessage) helper (PR #94) - it marks the file errored ('corrupt data in transit'), bounces the status back to Pending, toasts the failure, sends EVENT_RECEIVER_REJECT so the sender stops cleanly, and tears down the per-file chunk/stats/queue state and, since PR #133, the receivingFileGeneration entry - instead of the byte count never catching up and the file sitting in Processing forever; the EVENT_RECEIVED_CHUNK ack is sent only after successful decryption so a corrupt chunk never advances the sender.

The sender's document-level paste listener is scoped to file sharing: handlePasteEvent ignores events whose target is an INPUT, TEXTAREA, SELECT, or content-editable element, so pasting an answer code or custom ICE server value into any text field no longer silently adds a stray clipboard.txt to the sender file list, and onDestroy removes the listener so it never outlives the component.

Removing a file while its chunk pipeline is in flight is safe: onRemove sets the stop flag (when Processing) before deleting the entry; the async pipeline only ever dereferences the entry reference captured at onSend entry (never a live re-read of sendingFiles[key] after an await), re-checks stop and the live entry at every await boundary, and the event handlers bail when the live entry is gone - so no continuation can dereference a deleted entry (previously an uncaught TypeError from sendingFiles[key].aesKey/.progress) or send a chunk into the void; onContinue likewise refuses to re-enter the pipeline on a dead channel (channelSender.isLost()).

Because metaData.size is peer-controlled and is the receiver's completion gate, the receiver validates it with a lower bound and an integer bound: validateFileMetadata rejects a size that is not finite, is <= 0, or is not an integer (PR #127) with an explicit 'invalid file size' error (such a value would otherwise complete the file on the first chunk with a partial/empty payload, make the progress math NaN/negative and break the progress UI, or dead-end the transfer on a fractional size the exact-match gate can never satisfy), and the per-chunk progress ratio is clamped to [0, 100] before reaching the UI as defense in depth on top of the exact-match gate and the overshoot reject. Since PR #136 this clamp lives in the shared updateTransferProgress helper (src/utils/transferProgress.ts), so it is uniform for both the sender's sendNextChunk and the receiver's processChunk.

onAccept (the shared entry point of autoAccept and the list UI's Accept button) guards up front against metadata-failed entries — error set (key decryption or max-size validation), or an encrypted session with no aesKey (PR #78): it toasts 'Cannot accept <name>: the metadata/key failed to process — the sender must resend the file', sends EVENT_RECEIVER_REJECT, leaves the entry in WaitingAccept + error, and creates no chunk map (so late-arriving chunks are dropped by the onChunkData guard); without a usable key the transfer can never succeed — an encrypted session would either assemble the raw ciphertext as a Success blob or hit rejectCorruptChunk on every chunk (an N-toast storm per resend) — and only entries that pass the guard emit EVENT_RECEIVER_ACCEPT, flip to Processing, and get their chunk/stats maps.

The receiver's two reject paths (rejectOversizedStream for a stream that exceeds the declared metaData.size, rejectCorruptChunk for a chunk that fails AES-GCM auth) are thin wrappers over one shared rejectFile(id, receivingFile, error, toastMessage) helper (PR #94), which guards on receivingFileChunkMap[id] as source of truth (no-op if the file is no longer being actively received), sets the entry's error, bounces status to Pending, toasts, sends EVENT_RECEIVER_REJECT via the guarded send() so the sender bounces to Pending instead of reporting a successful transfer, and deletes the per-file chunk/stats/queue maps AND, since PR #133, the receivingFileGeneration entry (the delete sits after the sibling map deletes, and after the live-attempt guard, so a no-op reject never burns the entry); this deduplicated ~25 lines of copy-pasted teardown that had to stay in sync, and tests/receiver-metadata-size.test.mjs follows the delegation when extracting the rejectOversizedStream body.

The guarded data-channel send is one shared helper (PR #97): createChannelSender(dataChannel) in src/utils/channelSender.ts returns send(message) — false without touching the channel when the lost flag is set or readyState !== 'open', true on success, and on a throwing send it flips the lost flag and returns false instead of leaking InvalidStateError — plus idempotent markLost() (fired by onChannelClose on both sides) and isLost() (the helper's live read). The sender's connectionLost flag is a $state the template reacts to (flipped by onChannelClose() and by a thin send() wrapper mirroring isLost(), PR #109) that onContinue's dead-channel refusal and the file-list UI gate read — NOT a $derived over isLost(), which would cache false forever because isLost() reads a plain closure variable; the receiver gates on the helper's isLost() read directly. Sender.svelte and Receiver.svelte keep their call sites in the plain send(...) shape.

The sender rejects metadata-invalid files at pick time (PR #96): onFilesPick runs validateFileMetadata on each file's metadata before registering the entry, and a failure (the only reachable pick-time case is size <= 0 / non-finite — e.g. a 0-byte file) toasts the error and continues without registering, because such a file can never complete (the receiver bounces it with EVENT_VALIDATE_ERROR on every resend and processChunk's exact-match gate receivedSize === size can never be satisfied by an empty payload), so registering it as a Resend-able Pending entry was a guaranteed dead-end that re-fired a 'Receiver validate error' toast on every retry.

onMetaData's key-decryption SUCCESS path re-reads receivingFiles[id] and null-guards it after the async RSA decryption await before assigning aesKey (PR #101): the entry is deniable/removable during that window (the list UI shows Accept/Deny on WaitingAccept entries since PR #76; onDeny deletes the entry) and the previous unguarded `receivingFiles[id].aesKey = aesKey` threw 'Cannot set properties of undefined (setting aesKey)' as an unhandled rejection outside any try/catch when a Deny landed in the window — no toast, no error state, and no EVENT_VALIDATE_ERROR/EVENT_RECEIVER_REJECT for the sender. The guarded handler returns quietly for a removed entry; the sibling key-unwrap CATCH path's receivingFiles[id].error write is null-guarded separately in PR #103, so both post-await writes are now guarded. Pinned by tests/receiver-metadata-key-null-guard.test.mjs, which mirrors the pre-fix and post-fix shapes with a mocked decrypt that runs onRemove before it settles and statically guards the real component source.

onMetaData's key-decryption CATCH path (PR #103) re-reads receivingFiles[id] and null-guards it before the error write: when the entry was denied/removed during the decryption await, the catch returns quietly instead of throwing an unhandled TypeError on the receivingFiles[id].error assignment — the second unguarded post-await write in onMetaData, fixed after the success path's aesKey write (PR #101). Without the guard, a Deny landing in the decryption window would leave receivingFiles[id] undefined and the catch's error-assignment would throw 'Cannot set properties of undefined (setting error)' outside any try/catch, and the addToastMessage + send(EVENT_VALIDATE_ERROR) that follow would never run, leaving the sender's file stuck in WaitingAccept forever. Pinned by tests/receiver-metadata-key-catch-null-guard.test.mjs (a mocked decrypt that denies the entry mid-await plus a static guard on the real component).

createZipStoreOnly is a classic (no-zip64) store-only ZIP writer: it writes no zip64 extra fields, so every 32-bit size and offset must fit below 0x100000000; it throws explicitly when an entry is >= 4 GiB (0xffffffff, the 'size in zip64 extra' sentinel — which would otherwise wrap the 32-bit header fields with no such extra present, producing a silently corrupt archive) or when the archive's central directory starts past that value, instead of emitting a corrupt archive. The receiver 'Max Size' dropdown's largest option is therefore capped at 2 GB (below the 4 GiB ceiling), and DEFAULT_RECEIVE_OPTIONS.maxSize (1 GB) stays below it, so the default never allows a file the bulk 'Download all files (zip)' path cannot archive (PR #110).

A stop only matters while bytes remain to send: the RECEIVED_CHUNK ack handler bails on stop only when the closure's offset is still below metaData.size (a mid-file pause resets to Pending); a stop with offset >= size means every byte was delivered before the stop clicked (Stop during the final chunk's send/ack window), so the completion ack still finishes the entry to Success — otherwise the file stays stuck in Processing and a later Continue re-sends the last chunk, which the receiver's exact-size gate rejects as an overshoot on a fully delivered file. A completed (Success) entry is terminal: a stray or synthetic ack returns without bouncing it back to Pending, and stop is cleared on completion so the list never renders a Continue button for a finished entry.

sendBuffer reports whether the chunk actually hit the wire (true when send() ran, false when the stop check bailed before sending - the chunk is on the wire even if stop flipped between encryption finishing and the send), and sendNextChunk advances the closure's offset only when it did; skipping the bookkeeping on stop used to leave offset behind the wire after a stop during the final chunk's send/ack window, so a later Continue would re-slice and re-send the last bytes, which the receiver's exact-size gate rejects as an overshoot. Progress UI for a removed/aborted entry is cosmetic, so skipping it on stop is safe.

The 'Send all files' batch button is gated on the same connectionLost flag as every per-file send action (PR #111): with the channel lost it is a guaranteed silent no-op (send() no-ops and each onSend only re-stamps the connection-lost error plus one toast per pending file), so the template wraps it in {#if !connectionLost} leaving only Remove, and sendAllFiles() itself returns early on channelSender.isLost() as the code-level backstop mirroring onContinue's dead-channel refusal.

onAccept bails on a combined null + status guard before the ACCEPT send — `if (!receivingFile || receivingFile.status !== FileStatus.WaitingAccept) return;` (PR #117, src/components/receiver/Receiver.svelte:416): onAccept flips the entry to Processing only after the EVENT_RECEIVER_ACCEPT send and the Accept button is removed only on Svelte's next re-render, so a second Accept click in the same frame previously passed the bare null guard and fired a second EVENT_RECEIVER_ACCEPT while re-initializing receivingFileChunkMap / receivingFileStatsMap and deleting the chunkQueue entry; the sender's persistent ACCEPT handler (eventemitter3 .on, not .once) then fired sendNextChunk() concurrently, the same chunk went on the wire twice, receivedSize double-counted, and the exact-match gate was either never reached or crossed into rejectOversizedStream — a fully delivered file marked Success with duplicated bytes or rejected as oversized. The same guard also covers entries that onChannelClose already bounced to Pending (+error), where re-accepting would re-initialize chunk state for a file that can never complete. The guard runs before, and does not short-circuit, the metadata-failure reject branch. Pinned by tests/receiver-double-accept.test.mjs (377 lines, landed with PR #117): a pre-fix control proving the double click sends two EVENT_RECEIVER_ACCEPT, a post-fix no-op proof (exactly one ACCEPT, chunk map not recreated, a dead-channel Pending entry stays Pending with no ACCEPT sent), a metadata-failure WaitingAccept entry still rejecting via the PR #78 path, and static regex guards that the real onAccept carries the combined null+status guard after the entry capture and before the reject branch; tests/receiver-accept-removed-null-guard.test.mjs (PR #115) was updated so its static guard accepts either the standalone null check or the combined null+status guard.

The sender bitrate clock is reset at accept, not at the Send click (PR #121): onSend initializes the closure fileStats with startTime: Date.now() at click time, but the chunk pipeline only starts on the peer's EVENT_RECEIVER_ACCEPT, so any waiting-accept delay (e.g. Auto accept off) inflated the bitrate denominator and made 'Sending: X/sec' under-report real throughput for the whole transfer; the EVENT_RECEIVER_ACCEPT handler now writes fileStats.startTime = Date.now() so the denominator is time-since-ACCEPT, mirroring the receiver which starts receivingFiles[id].startTime in onAccept() - progress (an offset/size ratio) is unaffected. Since PR #134 the shared updateTransferProgress helper floors the elapsed denominator to a 1 ms minimum so a small file whose accept and first progress update share a millisecond no longer divides by 0 to Infinity, and since PR #136 the progress+bitrate write routes through that one helper at both call sites. Pinned by tests/sender-bitrate-clock.test.mjs and tests/bitrate-zero-elapsed-guard.test.mjs via static source inspection of both components plus the shared helper.

Incoming-file admission caps (PR #131) bound peer-driven resource exhaustion: before registering a new entry, onMetaData counts active (non-Success) entries against MAX_INCOMING_FILES (32) and the total declared size of every not-yet-removed entry against MAX_TOTAL_RECEIVED_BYTES (8 GiB); a frame that would exceed either is not registered and is rejected back to the sender with EVENT_RECEIVER_REJECT plus a single error toast. The frame's own id is excluded from both counts so a re-offer of an already-held file resets the same entry without counting against the caps, and the terminal-Success early-return runs before the caps so a completed id is never counted; the rendered toast list is separately bounded to the most recent MAX_VISIBLE_TOASTS (10) in Toast.svelte.
